Vishay is a speculative shadow candidate: U.S.-listed, underfollowed, and exposed to passives/server power, but direct high-end AI-server MLCC qualification evidence is missing.
TDK is relevant beyond MLCCs because AI-server board-level passive constraints include MLCCs, power inductors, sensors, and compact power-conversion components.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics has strong direct evidence for AI-server MLCCs and silicon capacitors, but no clean U.S.-listed/OTC candidate ticker was verified in the supplied context; revisit in non-US or ETF-exposure pass.
Keep MRAAY and TTDKY as reference anchors for AI-server MLCC product requirements, demand commentary, and pricing/capacity signals.
Add VSH to the underfollowed lane as a mid-cap US-listed diversified passives supplier with MLCC and low-ESR product evidence; AI-server exposure remains unverified.
Add KN to the underfollowed lane as a mid-cap specialty capacitor and precision-device supplier; direct AI-server exposure is a hypothesis requiring design-win or customer evidence.

The strongest validated node claim is that AI-server power systems require high-capacitance-density, low-ESR, low-ESL MLCCs deployed in large parallel counts, especially around 48V-to-12V power conversion and accelerator-board decoupling.

Need to verify whether US-listed smaller suppliers actually qualify into NVIDIA GB200/GB300, hyperscaler, ODM, or AI accelerator reference designs; product catalog fit alone is insufficient for Layer 2 survival.
MRAAY should remain the reference anchor for AI-server high-end MLCC validation, but not the main alpha-hunt target because the name is already being discussed in AI-passive-component narratives.
VSH is a plausible underfollowed US-listed MLCC/passives candidate; direct AI-server qualification evidence is still missing and should be a Layer 2 priority.

KN is a plausible specialty-capacitor shadow candidate after Cornell Dubilier, but its exposure may be defense/industrial/medical rather than AI servers unless data-center or HPC design wins are verified.
BELFB belongs in the adjacent chokepoint lane for data-center power magnetics, inductors, chokes, and power shelves rather than as a direct MLCC supplier.

Need a separate non-US/ADR mapping for Samsung Electro-Mechanics, TDK, Taiyo Yuden, Yageo, Kyocera/AVX, and Walsin because several likely direct MLCC suppliers are not clean US-listed small/mid-cap candidates.

The working bottleneck is still a hypothesis: proof requires evidence of high-end MLCC lead-time extension, price increases, capacity allocation, customer qualification constraints, or explicit AI-server/HPC demand commentary from suppliers.
